text: The first was a prince named Siddhartha Gautama, born around two and a half thousand years ago in Lumbini, in today's Nepal.
The story goes that his father, a king, wanted him to see nothing sad, no sickness, no old age, no death, just a perfect palace.
But one day, Siddhartha slipped out, and he saw an old man, a sick man, a dead body, and
a calm wandering monk. One afternoon outside the palace, that's all it took. At 29, he
left his palace, his wife and his baby son, to find out why people suffer. After years
Years of searching, he sat under a fig tree at Bodh Gaya and, tradition says, refused
to get up until he understood.
When he rose, he was the Buddha, the awakened one.
He gave his first sermon at Sarnath, near Varanasi.
His answer was a middle way, not luxury, not starving yourself, a calm, kind, disciplined
Around the same time, another prince, Mahavira, gave up his throne too.
He taught Ahimsa, non-violence to every living thing, and shaped the religion of Jainism.
Two princes, zero palaces, very confused royal parents.
